text:
The halogen bulb above David Vance’s desk shuddered, casting a strobe of light across the faded blueprint pinned to the corkboard. It was the original diagram for the old Blackwood Point lighthouse, a structure long since declared unsafe. A persistent, almost musical hum had taken residence in the building’s wiring all day, a fragile thing that now threatened to snap, plunging the office into the kind of deep gloom Blackwood Bay specialized in.

Just as the hum seemed to waver on the brink of silence, a low, deep vibration began to pulse up through the floorboards. It wasn't violent, just a pervasive tremor, as if the entire town was exhaling, or perhaps bracing. A half-empty mug of cold coffee shimmied an inch across the blotter. Vance’s eyes, however, stayed fixed on the blueprint. He traced a finger along the spiral staircase detail, noticing for the first time a series of hairline fractures marked in red pencil, almost invisible under the shifting light. The town, like the paper beneath his hand, felt brittle, about to give.
